description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs lines 317-331: The DFS_BUDGET (10,000 visits) is shared across all iterative-deepening rounds (1..=10 depth). Each call to dfs() at depth 1 explores the same nodes as depth 2, then depth 3, etc. For a pool of N candidate CA certs, the first round visits O(N) nodes, the second O(N²), etc. The shared budget means that for a legitimate pool of even 20-30 CA certs, the budget may be exhausted before the correct depth is reached, returning BudgetExceeded even though a valid path exists.

Example: 30 CA certs all with matching subject names. Round 1: 30 visits. Round 2: 30 + 30*30 = 930 visits. Round 3: 930 + 30*30*30 = ~27,930 visits total — BudgetExceeded on round 3 for a pool of 30 certs, even though valid paths at depth 1 may exist.

The correct fix is either: (a) reset budget per round, (b) use a per-round budget, or (c) document the effective pool size limit. The DFS_BUDGET=10,000 comment says "10,000 visits is sufficient for legitimate chains" but provides no analysis of pool size limits. A pool of 30 intermediate CAs with identical subject DNs (not uncommon in large enterprise PKI with many issuing CAs under the same root) could exhaust the budget.
title: P2: build_path budget shared across iterative-deepening rounds — BudgetExceeded may fire on legitimate chains
